LIVE WEIGHTS
Generation settings

Checking live model tools…

How the context window works

The window is the number of recent tokens used for each prediction, not words or output length. Smaller windows lose context sooner. The model forgets the excluded prefix, including the beginning of a long prompt.

What changes when the window slides?

Each forward pass sees only the latest selected tokens. Their learned position indices restart at 0 inside that window. Discarded tokens leave no hidden-state memory. This is an inference technique; it does not train a model with a longer context. Longer output may still lose consistency or stop early at EOS.

With Sliding window off, the model uses its fixed 128-position context. The prompt including BOS must be shorter than 128 tokens. The window-length input applies only when Sliding window is selected.

Choose a display speed, then generate. You can change the speed while tokens appear.

Generation details

Continue a story with the current language model. Compare an isolated random model using the same prompt, temperature and sampling seed. Generation leaves the training state unchanged.

EOS ends generation immediately. Maximum new tokens (1–1000) is an upper limit, not a target length. There is no minimum length to fill. Fixed mode also stops at the 128-position context boundary; sliding mode can continue beyond that boundary.

Pause changes display only; GPU output can continue to buffer. Stop keeps visible text and discards hidden tokens.

One displayed unit is one actual model token, not a word. Temperature 0 selects the most probable token. The first generated EOS ends the output, even on the last allowed token. Without EOS, generation stops at the maximum token limit or the fixed-context boundary when sliding is off. Small-model text may remain repetitive or incoherent.

Where does this training result go?

Data & targets, One update and Try the current model use the live language-model weights. Inspection and generation reveal what those actual weights predict.

Live Transfer starts from a copy of your current weights. Start a comparison in Transfer, fine-tune both branches, then classify a review. The copied source LM step stays fixed; each branch has its own fine-tuning steps. Later language-model updates do not change that copy.

Save current model explicitly saves both models and their training state. Refreshing the page retains the running session. Unsaved work can be lost when the trainer restarts or a model is reset. Recorded comparisons are separate saved experiments.

How the two branches are compared

Both branches get the same fresh classifier head, batches and optimizer settings. The random branch starts without language-model training. All backbone and head parameters are fine-tuned. Improvement is measured, never guaranteed.

Why supervised fine-tuning?

Language modeling learns to predict text. Sentiment training teaches a new classifier head to map the final [CLS] representation to negative or positive. Its gradients also adapt the copied transformer.

The random branch uses classification loss. The pretrained branch optionally adds language-model loss with λ = 0.5. Extra pretraining compute is part of the cost of that branch.
